This happened today. I went to the park with my GF and 4 month puppy to have fun and do some training. After some time a very pretty but unsupervised Husky dog (this is Poland, so these dogs are kinda uncommon here) comes up to us. I'm really hesitant, since I don't know the dog, and don't know how it will react to our pup. THANKFULLY he's timid, and they do their dog greetings and whatnot.

Then the owners come up, a Korean pair. We greet and laugh at how the small corgi and a Big Husky dogs plays. We talk, and it turns out that the Husky is only 7 months old. I tell them that we need to go, but I see the owner struggling really hard to keep control of him. I ask him if he went with the dog to puppy school, or done any training, and turns out he didn't. Most good dog owners would be really mad at this point - letting a untrained big dog run wild on the park like that.

Instead, I asked showed him how to work with the dog, how to concentrate him on the owner, make him walk with the owner and not pull on the leash. It was really hard, since my corgi, Zelda weighs 5kg, but the husky was probably thrice that if not more, and had a LOT of strength with that too. It really made me think how easy I have it, and how well behaved Zelda is :D After that I gave them the number to a local dog school, and wished them the best of luck.

tl;dr: Helped inexperienced dog owners
